newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebel authorities in Zaire delay refugee airlift.
newsitem.headline: Rebel authorities in Zaire delay refugee airlift.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency said rebel authorities on Friday ordered an indefinite delay to a U.N. operation to airlift 100,000 Rwandan refugees home because of cholera fears.
"The authorities have delayed the operation until further notice," said Paul Stromberg, a UNHCR spokesman in Kisangani.
"We will move forward the minute we have the local authorities act on the medical opinion that the people from Biaro camp can travel but we don't know when that will be," he added.

Biaro camp, 42 km (25 miles) south of Kisangani, was the site from which UNHCR planned to take the first 80 refugee children and truck them to Kisangani airport for a flight to the eastern city of Goma.
Earlier on Friday, hundreds of angry Zaireans stopped aid workers from reaching two camps for 80,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees and UNHCR said it was temporarily suspending its operations.
The demonstrators prevented an aid convoy from leaving a ferry over the Zaire river, attacked vehicles and threatened aid workers in a protest over the refugees and the aid they are receiving.
UNHCR had planned to start the airlift on Friday but on Thursday delayed it until Saturday because rebel authorities were concerned the operation might spread cholera to the city.

A total of 330 cholera cases and 19 cholera deaths have been registered among 50,000 refugees at Kasese camp, 29 km (17 miles) south of Kisangani. About 30,000 refugees are camped at Biaro and another 20,000 are scattered further south.
UNHCR officials said they would only move healthy refugees and would wait until the sick recovered before airlifting them.
The refugees are the rump of more than two million Hutus who fled Rwanda in 1994 after the victory of Tutsi rebels in the civil war and the genocide of 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates.

The refugees are in a very poor state after trekking about 600 km (375 miles) since last October through dense jungle where they survived on grubs and tree-bark. They marched westwards to flee Tutsi-dominated rebels, supported by Rwanda's government.

In another development, the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) said some 300 Zaireans armed with machetes and clubs overpowered guards at a WFP warehouse in Kisangani on Friday and looted 15 tonnes of food, enough to feed up to 30,000 people for one day.
A WFP spokeswoman said Zaireans also tried to loot a second WFP warehouse in Kisangani but were kept away by guards. She said two Zairean loaders were beaten by the would-be looters.
"If we cannot get security guarantees, this will effect the amount of food coming in," said the spokesman, adding refugees at Biaro had enough food for the next two days and at Kasese for a week.
